Curriculum prints the current sequence in full and does not print a step count,' matching the body's printed 'ideate → brainstorm → plan → work → review → polish → compound → repeat' exactly (verified: body prints no step count, no 'four-step' language survives anywhere in the doc — checked ~line 159, which now reads 'Klaassen's loop at M1 resolves "I don't know where compounding starts" — the student sees the whole arc and the one stage they are standing in,' the 'four-step' qualifier removed). (2) Plan-as-loop-stage vs 'no plan mode in M1' — doc now carries an explicit carve-out (~line 159, M1-detail section): '**Not a conflict: `plan` is one of the stage names inside Klaassen's printed loop at M1.** Naming a stage in someone else's loop is not teaching the plan-mode primitive, and the M1 body neither invokes it nor explains it. Recorded 2026-08-02 so an audit does not re-flag the word.' This directly closes the M2-plan-mode-contrast concern this judge raised last cycle; the exercise body doesn't invoke or explain plan mode anywhere (verified body lines 1-44). (3) Klaassen-attribution timing — doc's design statement (~line 276-278) now reads 'Klaassen attribution lands in Ex3's own body, where the loop is printed, and the retro prompt then confirms it rather than revealing it,' replacing the prior 'attribution happens inside Claude's Ex3 retro summary... peer recognition, not a lecture' framing that the body had already outgrown. Worth surfacing if they fit: Cherny, Klaassen, Ronacher, Pocock, Karpathy, Willison' — now correctly read as confirmation of a name the student already has, not the sole reveal. Separately (not one of the three strategy conflicts, but this judge's own locatability finding): 'compound' is now bolded inside the printed sequence (line 9: '...polish → **compound** → repeat'), which is exactly the fix this judge's own prior fix_hint proposed ('keep compound as the visually terminal or bolded word'). Regenerated trace confirms phase 1 mood_score moves 7→8 on this basis (see mood_summary). Flagged, non-blocking for THIS file: the same strategy-doc passage that closes conflict (3) also names a fresh cost it does NOT resolve — 'the reveal is now spent before the M1 closer reaches it, so how-this-training-was-built can no longer stage "the pattern has a name" as new information, and its maintainer claim that Klaassen is named once on the student surface is false until that lecture is reworked.' That is a real, currently-true inconsistency, but it lives in a DIFFERENT file (how-this-training-was-built.md), is explicitly logged by the maintainer as 'the cost is real and is the accepted trade' (not a fresh oversight), and this run is scoped to compound-and-close.md, which now matches its strategy doc exactly. Recommend a follow-up story-class fire on how-this-training-was-built.md before ship, but that is a TODO on that file, not a blocking finding here.
